AfterObtained.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the pull CAN apply RelicModel.IsAllowed now. RunState.pull_relic_from_front (sts2_rl/run.py:731) calls _drop_disallowed_from_grab_bag (sts2_rl/run.py:769-776) first, which drops every relic whose `Relic.is_allowed(run)` (sts2_rl/relics/base.py:198) is False -- the port of RelicGrabBag.RemoveDisallowedRelicsFromDeques (RelicGrabBag.cs:250-271) that RelicFactory.PullNextRelicFromFront goes through. Large Capsule's two pulls therefore see the same bag the game would. WAS: `sts2_rl.relics.base.Relic` declared no is_allowed member and pull_relic_from_front applied no such filter, so the two relics could be ones the game had removed from the bag.

guards.what: N1: `GetStrikeForCharacter` / `GetDefendForCharacter` fork on `TestMode.IsOn` (LargeCapsule.cs:38-54) -- PROMPT.md bug class 18
guards.rationale: The test arm returns ModelDb.Card<StrikeIronclad>/<DefendIronclad> for the Deprived test character; the SHIPPING arm is `character.CardPool.AllCards.First(c => c.Rarity == CardRarity.Basic && c.Tags.Contains(CardTag.Strike|Defend))`. TestMode.TurnOnInternal (TestMode.cs:38) is documented 'NEVER CALL THIS' and has no caller under src/, so shipping always takes the second arm -- checked BEFORE reading, per class 18, because relic/calling_bell shipped the test arm. For the Ironclad the two arms COINCIDE, and the sim's `make_card('strike')` / `make_card('defend')` is right either way: EXECUTED, the ported Basic-rarity cards are [('bash', []), ('defend', ['defend']), ('strike', ['strike']), ('sweep', [])], so the tag filter has exactly one match each. The character-pool half is Ironclad-only by construction and is a waiver for other characters under the shared contract's global scope.

The no-rarity overload is `PullNextRelicFromFront(player, RollRarity(player), _ => true)` (RelicFactory.cs), and RollRarity(player) draws one NextFloat off `player.PlayerRng.Rewards`. run.obtain_relic_from_grab_bag (run.py:631-636) calls pull_relic_from_front with no rarity, which rolls on `self.rewards_rng` -- the same stream by that method's own documented default (run.py:576-584) -- and then adds the relic through add_relic, which is RelicCmd.Obtain's after_obtained dispatch. So both the draw count and the stream match, and the project's 'Relic rarity rolls on Rewards' note holds. EXECUTED: 2 pulls, bag 96 -> 94. Rule 7: run.py is not hashed by this record.

The no-index Add overload appends at the END of the deck (AddInternal with no index), which is the placement audit/records/seam/creature_card_cmds.json pins for out-of-combat pile adds and which run.transform_card's docstring (run.py:418-428) calls parity-critical because the combat-start UnstableShuffle is order-dependent. EXECUTED here rather than asserted, which is what audit/records/relic/arcane_scroll.json could not do from its own two files: the deck tail after the pickup is ['strike', 'defend'] in that order, i.e. appended, Strike first. add_card also runs modify_card_being_added_to_deck and after_card_added_to_deck (run.py:341-354), the two hooks CardPileCmd.Add runs (CardPileCmd.cs:501, 635) -- so unlike relic/leafy_poultice's transform path this relic does not drop them. Rule 7: run.py and cards/pool.py are not hashed here.

guards.rationale: C# `RelicCmd.Obtain(relic, Owner)` fires the granted relic's AfterObtained, and run.add_relic does the same (run.py:550-552), so a pulled Lee's Waffle or Looming Fruit applies its max HP here on both sides.
